name: IC Memo Builder

inputs.name: Deal basics: target, sector, deal type, stage in process

steps.title: Lead with the decision
steps.detail: What is the IC being asked to approve, at what valuation, by when? First half-page.

steps.title: Structure the thesis
steps.detail: 2-4 pillars, each with evidence and the diligence item that would confirm or kill it.

steps.title: Present returns honestly
steps.detail: Base/downside/upside with drivers, not just the base MOIC. Show what breaks the deal.

steps.title: Pre-empt the questions
steps.detail: Every IC has predictable attacks: customer concentration, cyclicality, management, exit. Answer them before they’re asked.

steps.title: Flag the unknowns
steps.detail: Open diligence items with owners and dates. Hiding unknowns is how memos lose credibility.

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Assembling section drafts from your model, CIM notes and diligence materials

steps.title: Delegate 2
steps.detail: Formatting the returns and sensitivity exhibits

sections.name: IC memo skeleton with drafted sections
sections.detail: Structure a PE investment committee memo: deal summary, investment thesis, market, financials, returns, risks and diligence status — organised around the decisions the IC needs to make, not around everything you know.

outputs.sourcePolicy: Every figure cites the page or filing it was read from; nothing is stated without a source.

verification.description: Numbers in prose match the model exhibits exactly
Claimed market data traces to a named source
Thesis pillars and risk section don’t silently contradict each other
The ask is explicit on page one
Each thesis pillar maps to a diligence item
Downside case is a real scenario, not base-minus-10%

humanCheckpoints: Which risks are deal-breakers vs priced-in
What you’re asking the IC for: approval, guidance or more time

display.jobToBeDone: Draft a first-pass investment committee memo that anticipates the committee’s questions.
